name: Bun quay
summary: Rice-flour noodles in a stirred broth with fish, shrimp, squid, herbs, and onion, eaten with a dip you mix yourself from chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus. The sauce comes out zesty, sweet, salty, and sour at once.
origin: Phu Quoc. The bowl was brought from central Vietnam in 1955 and was known as bún tôm until 1996.
history: The early bowl was ground shrimp from central Vietnam in 1955. It was called bún tôm until 1996, when the Kiến Xây family tried the island’s seafood and local seasonings. From 1996 to 2012 that family’s kitchen was known across Vietnam for the bowl. The dish is now cooked in other regions, and the island is where it started.
culture: It is a morning dish by tradition, and it is now served through the day and into the evening. The island has over ten rooms. Eat it on Long Beach or in Dương Đông.
taste: The sauce is chili, sugar, fish sauce, and citrus: zest, sweet, salty, and sour.
howToEat: Stir your sauce first, then eat the noodles, fish, shrimp, squid, herbs, and onion with it.
It is a morning bowl by tradition, and the island now serves it through the day and into the evening.
where: Dương Đông, on the street across from the harbour, and along Long Beach. The island has over ten bún quây rooms.
seoTitle: Bun quay in Phu Quoc — the stirring noodle bowl
seoDescription: Bún quây is Phu Quoc’s stirred noodle bowl: rice-flour noodles, fish, shrimp, and squid, with a chili, sugar, fish-sauce, and citrus dip you mix yourself.
